chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Wear the white, for it is better and purer, and enshroud your deceased in it.'

key_terms.أَطْهَرُ: Purer, more ritually clean — from the root ط ه ر (tahara), the same root as taharah (ritual purity)
key_terms.أَطْيَبُ: Better, more pleasant, more wholesome — from the root ط ي ب (tayyib), implying spiritual purity and physical cleanliness
key_terms.الْبَيَاضَ: White clothing; referring to undyed white fabric, which was common and highly regarded in early Islamic Arabia
key_terms.كَفِّنُوا: Enshroud (imperative plural) — referring to wrapping the deceased in the kafan (burial shroud) before interment
key_terms.مَوْتَاكُمْ: Your deceased; the plural of mayyit (dead person), grammatically possessive to the community

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about wearing white clothes in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) transmits a prophetic hadith in which the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) recommends wearing white clothing, describing it as both superior in quality and purer in nature. The instruction extends beyond daily dress to include the funerary shroud (kafan), making white the prescribed colour for enshrouding the deceased. This hadith is foundational to Islamic jurisprudence on recommended dress and burial practices, establishing white as the preferred colour for both the living and the dead.
